As Mark Zuckerberg dives deeper into Meta's AI investments, the stock keeps sinking.

$META has closed in the red for 10 days in a row, continuing it's longest streak ever. yhoo.it/4pMQXCX

When Mark Zuckerberg is asked if we're nearing an AI breakthrough on Meta's earnings call, he says plenty has already broken through — but new capabilities are always coming as cycles accelerate.

Video

Mark Zuckerberg says Meta is "investing aggressively" in AI infrastructure, highlighting its massive data center deal with BlackRock in El Paso, Texas.

Video

Mark Zuckerberg breaks down Meta's AI roadmap on the company's Q2 earnings call.

"Overall, we expect that a significant portion of our compute is going to go towards training our models, growing our core business and delivering personal agents and new products," Zuckerberg adds.

Video
Despite Meta missing its Q2 earnings per share estimates, CEO Mark Zuckerberg remains focused on the big picture. yhoo.it/4pMQXCX
$MSFT Q4 earnings beat investor expectations, driven by an increase in Azure revenue.

$META missed earnings expectations but beat on revenue in Q2 while narrowing its 2026 capital expenditure outlook. 

Shares fell nearly 8% in after-hours trading. yhoo.it/4pMQXCX

$MSFT earnings
💵 Revenue: $90.01B vs $87.7B expected
💲 EPS: $4.74 vs $4.25

$META Q2 earnings 
💵 Revenue: $60.8B vs $60.24B expected
💸 Full-year capex: $130B to $145B vs $125B to $145B previously

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh says the AI capex boom is driving manufacturing momentum, but predicting its ultimate impact on the economy isn't so simple.

Video

Post-Warsh comments: The bond curve is steepening hard, the 30-year just crossed 5.2 for the first time since June 2007.

Market may be deciding to handle inflation itself, forget the Fed.

Fed meetings under Kevin Warsh are a good family fight.

Video
Top takeaway from press conference two for Fed chair Kevin Warsh: my steak won’t be any cheaper this summer.
Fed Chairmain Kevin Warsh weighed in on the "remarkable" growth in AI tech spending and why it’s keeping the Fed on its toes. yhoo.it/4yOomRR

Kevin Warsh commits to press conferences for the rest of 2026.

Video

"We're in the performance business," says Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh. 

Adding: "We've got no magic wand, this isn't something that we're going to be able to carry out in days or weeks, but we're going to deliver on the responsibility that Congress gave us."
